verification.reason: In ResultsLock.take, writeFileSync with flag "wx" on an existing FIFO path fails with EEXIST. claimant then calls openSync(path, O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW) with no O_NONBLOCK. That blocks synchronously until a writer opens the FIFO, so measureParity hangs instead of refusing. Nothing checks the file type before the open, and fstatSync(...).isFile() only runs after the open returns. The probe copied these exact calls and hung again, which matches this reading of the code. It did not run measureParity, but take calls claimant directly on the EEXIST path. The failure is a hang, not a fail-open, and it needs someone to have created a FIFO at the lock path. That makes the impact modest, but the defect is real.

The check does pass for a dangling link, as the probe shows. But the run never writes through the link, so nothing lands in the checkout. The probe replicated the resolution and then called writeFileSync(path) on the link itself. The real code doesn't do that. ResultsLock.take puts the lock at `<scratch>/out.json.lock`, which is outside the checkout. save() writes `${out}.${pid}.tmp` with flag "wx", which is a new file beside the link in scratch. It then calls renameSync(tmp, out). rename replaces the symlink entry and doesn't follow it, so repo/new.json is never created. The only writeFileSync calls in parity.ts are the lock write (line 473) and the temp write (line 716). The probe's "wrote inside checkout" comes from its own direct write and shows nothing about the code under review.
